label: the wrench (models/v_crowbar.mdl, models/p_crowbar.mdl, models/w_crowbar.mdl): a pipe wrench: red-painted handle worn to bare iron, a heavy toothed jaw

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_crowbar.mdl, models/w_satchel.mdl, models/w_357.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, A, B, C where the asset was D, B, D, A: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Against the brief's words (a pipe wrench: red handle, heavy toothed jaw), every view reads as a toothed block head on a long handle. Nothing sticks out or is missing in the side, top, below or angled views. The jaw is a squared box rather than a pipe wrench's angled jaw, but the brief does not name that form.

M2.reason: Measured length 19.2 units against the brief's 18, 6.9% off (within 15%). Width 4 and height 8.7 are not asked for by the brief.

M3.reason: The parts the brief names are both there: the handle (a red tapered shaft in every side view) and the toothed jaw (rows of small teeth on one face, visible in top, below, front and in-hand views). The bare-iron wear is a paint detail, charged to M5. The adjusting nut and hinge of a real pipe wrench are not named by the brief and not in the Valve line-up, so they are not charged.

M4.reason: The handle is a saturated red painted metal and the jaw a grey steel, the two materials the brief names. The regions match in the first-person and in-hand views. The missing wear is charged to M5.

M5.reason: The brief asks for the red handle worn to bare iron. In all ten w_ views and in the first-person view the handle is an unbroken red with no bare steel patch, rim or scuff. The jaw has only its tooth notches, with no wear or panel detail to show the worn, heavy look the brief describes.

M6.reason: Measured line-up: the three Valve originals were picked for the odd one out, and the asset (D) was never picked in four readings (C, A, B, C against asset positions D, B, D, A), so the test passed. The score is capped at 2 by the rubric. The asset is flatter and blockier than the crowbar beside it, but it reads as a Valve tool at that size.

M7.reason: The brief names no front. In the side views the w_ model lies along its length with the jaw at one end, and nothing in the front, top or below views shows it floating or sunk. Nothing visible is wrong.

M8.reason: SMAK checkErrors is empty. Triangles are 80, below twice the Half-Life median of the kind (2 x 142 = 284) and the three-quarter mark (187). Across the side, top and below views the jaw and handle read as closed solids, with the handle joined to the jaw end and nothing floating.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the wrench sits centre-left and low, handle pointing up and the jaw at the bottom edge, while the game's crowbar sits at the right with its business end up. So the wrench is not where the original sits and is turned the other way round, with the jaw where the grip should be. In attack.png no hands are visible, so the weapon never visibly parts from them; the frames show it swinging and changing size without a departure shown.
